chunks: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the adulterer — how should he be flogged? He said: The most intense of the flogging. I said: From over his clothes? He said: Rather, his clothes are stripped off.
I said: And the slanderer (false accuser of adultery)? He said: He is struck between the two strokes — his whole body is struck over his clothes.

key_terms.الزَّانِي: al-zani — the one who commits zina (fornication/adultery), subject to the hadd punishment of 100 lashes (unmarried) or rajm (married)
key_terms.الضَّرْبَيْنِ: al-darabayn — the two types of striking: intense (for zina) and moderate (for qadhf); the slanderer receives a punishment between these
key_terms.الْجَلْدُ: al-jald — flogging/lashing, the prescribed corporal punishment (hadd) for zina among unmarried persons
key_terms.الْمُفْتَرِي: al-muftar — the slanderer, one who falsely accuses a chaste person of zina, subject to 80 lashes (hadd al-qadhf)

ai.seo_question: According to Imam Kadhim, how is the hadd punishment for adultery administered differently from the hadd for slander in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) specifies the method of administering the hadd punishment for adultery (zina) and for slander (qadhf, falsely accusing someone of adultery). For the adulterer, the punishment must be carried out at maximum severity with clothes removed to ensure full effect. For the slanderer, a moderate punishment is prescribed — the whole body is struck but over the clothes, indicating a less severe application than for zina. This legal ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential distinction in hadd application, where the nature of the crime determines the manner of corporal punishment, a concern also addressed in classical fiqh texts.
